notes.text: Floor 1 is built with 6 cards, not the rulebook's 10: band 1 of the proposed list holds only 5 Room cards (3 Security Turnstile, 2 Flooded Ventilation Shaft) plus the Stairwell. The rulebook says nothing about a short pool, and the floor is legal as built, but this is a quarter of the 24 rooms issue 66 asks band 1 to hold. Cleared rooms leave the pool for the rest of the run, so floors 2 and 3 will be thinner still.

Turn 2 and the Stairwell is already up: a 6-card floor deck makes that a 1-in-5 chance each flip. Oomph 8 or Scramble 8 is out of reach for the starter hands alone (Red's best five cards make Oomph 8 only with both Overdrives, Exhausting 4; Gray's make Scramble 6). The Grav Harness Red bought last turn is what makes it reachable: its Scramble 3 plus Pick The Lock and Duck Under is 9. Going for the Scramble line, which also pays a Good Stuff.

That Exhaust took Hack the Doors, the reward Gray chose two turns ago, and it was no surprise in hindsight: Gray's deck held exactly one card, and I could have worked out which. The Scramble 3 line would have cleared this room for free with Coil Of Cable. I paid two Stamina for a Duct Tape and lost the better card. A player's mistake, not the game's, but it shows how 0.2's permanent Exhaust punishes a known top card: with a one-card deck, 'Exhaust 1' is a targeted loss, not a random one.

Settle your Stuff asks about Grav Harness again, one floor after Red paid a Shove to keep it. So rent is due every Ascend: each Good Stuff kept costs one starter card per floor, and a floor here is one to four turns long. Gray is holding five Good Stuff and eight non-Stuff cards; keeping all five would leave three starters and make next floor's rent unpayable. Stuff reads as a loan against Stamina, not deck growth. Keeping four of Gray's five and returning Emergency Power Core, whose Exhaust 2 per play is a second Stamina cost on top of the rent.

Rent is a swap, not a loss, while a weaker starter is left to Scrap: keeping Duct Tape & Wire (cost 1, 2/2) by Scrapping Lean In (cost 1, 1/1) improves Red's deck at the same card count. After this Ascend Red has no Lean In or Overdrive left and Gray is down to one Pick The Lock, so next floor's rent comes out of good cards. Three floors in eight turns; band 2 starts on floor 4 with rooms asking 7 to 11 per stat.

Hack the Doors reads 'Look at top 3 cards of any deck, put back in any order.' I played it to look at the Floor deck and put Gears & Glitch where I wanted it, and the engine asked only 'Look at the top 3 of whose deck?' with Red or Gray as the choices. The rulebook's table has three kinds of face-down deck (Character deck, Reward pool, Floor deck) and the glossary calls the Floor deck a deck. Suspected engine mismatch, or a rulebook question: does 'any deck' on a card mean the character decks only?

Junk Launcher counted a payer that was not its own. Red paid Charge In and Reckless Swing for it (pool Oomph 6, as printed: 2 plus 2 per card), then paid Grav Harness for Duct Tape & Wire, and the pool went to 10, not 8: Junk Launcher gained another 2 for the card spent on Duct Tape. The printed text (cards.yaml) is 'This card gains Oomph +2 for each card spent to play it this turn'; the old wording counted every card paid this turn. Suspected engine mismatch with the reworded card. It did not change this room's outcome.

The rent makes a character's card count invariant at Ascend: keeping k Good Stuff Scraps k non-Stuff cards, so Gray leaves this floor with 5 cards plus the reward whether she keeps zero of her seven Stuff or five. Stuff never grows the deck; it only replaces starters, and the reward card is the whole of a floor's Stamina growth. Gray has 5 non-Stuff cards and 7 Stuff, so at most five can be kept and next floor's rent would then have nothing to Scrap. Keeping the four best plus In Step.

Overgrown Hydroponics Bay prints Scramble 6 (Clear, but both get Bad Stuff) and Scramble 11 (Clear, and both get Good Stuff) as two challenges, not two thresholds of one. Under the Outcome rule both resolve at Scramble 11, so the best line still hands out two Bad Stuff. If the two lines were one challenge, only the 11 would resolve. Question for the designer: is the spore cloud meant to hit you even when you clear it cleanly? The cards.yaml shape follows the proposal as written; this is the first room where the challenge-versus-threshold distinction changes what a card does.

Grav Harness asked 'Who draws a card?' and offered only Red. Gray's deck was empty but her discard pile held 4 cards. The rulebook's Empty deck keyword says a draw with an empty deck first shuffles the discard pile into a new deck, and Turn Start draws did exactly that for Gray two turns ago. So Gray should have been a legal choice. Suspected engine mismatch: a mid-Play draw choice excludes a character with an empty deck and a non-empty discard. I wanted Gray to draw for the Scramble; choosing Red instead.

Spore Cloud (Holding: at Cleanup, discard down to 3) was in Gray's hand at Cleanup and Gray finished the turn holding 4: Distract & Pivot, Spore Cloud, Automated Salvage Kit and Riot Shield. Riot Shield returned to hand in the same Cleanup, so either Spore Cloud fired first on a 3-card hand and then Riot Shield came back, or it did not fire at all; the log shows no Spore Cloud discard either way. Rulebook question: in what order do 'at Cleanup' Holding effects and 'at the end of the turn' returns resolve? Also: Panic in Red's hand now shows every threshold with '+2 Scramble (printed N)', which reads clearly.

Red's Ascend offer is two cards, not three: the proposed Red reward pool holds nine cards and Red has taken seven in five floors (five Ascends plus two Hub rewards). Gray's pool of ten is at seven taken. By floor 6 both pools will be empty and Ascending will pay nothing. Under the rent invariant the reward card is a character's only Stamina growth, so an empty pool means the deck can only shrink from here. Keeping Panic rather than shedding it: shedding Scraps a real card, holding a dead one costs nothing until it is drawn.

Laser Grid Security Hall on floor 7: Scramble 14 or Oomph 18, Flee is both Exhaust 4. Gray has 5 live cards and all 5 are in hand, so a Flee would Exhaust from an empty deck and an empty discard and put her Down. Six floors of rent and a ten-card reward pool that is now empty have left Gray with exactly the Stamina one Flee costs. Clearing is the only move.

Laser Grid's 'Gray reveals a card reward' resolved to nothing: Gray's reward pool is empty (all ten cards taken by floor 6) and the log printed no line saying so. The rulebook does not say what an empty reward pool does; the outcome just vanished. Rulebook question, and a CLI note: an outcome that does nothing should say so. Bio-Hazard Containment Vault's room rule shows up as 'scrap <character> <card> for <stat>' in the moves hint, which is how I would have expected to find it.

Seven floors in twenty turns, and the decks are gone: after this Ascend Red has five cards plus Panic and Gray has two, In Step and Riot Shield. Neither pool has a reward left, so both decks can only shrink. Gray's best turn is now In Step paid with her other card, about Scramble 6, so the Monolith Core's Oomph 10 and Scramble 10 is out of reach and so is the Sentinel's. The run did not die of Exhaust; it died of rent on a reward pool that ran out on floor 6. Both of us will play floor 8 as far as it goes.

Gray went Down at Turn Start, not to a Flee. She had two live cards, drew both, and the third draw of 'draw up to five' found an empty deck and an empty discard pile, which the Empty deck keyword says is Down. So under 0.2 as written, holding fewer than five cards in deck and discard together is death at the next Turn Start, before any room is faced. The engine did what the rulebook says. Question for the designer: is a Turn Start draw with nothing left to draw meant to put a character Down, or does 'draw up to five' stop when the cards run out? The Stamina line in About the game ('if you need a card and have none left, you go Down') reads either way.
